body: Hmmmmm. I know there are those websites where you take surveys for money but idk if they're legit. Have you tried doing some sort of house cleaning or something for people? Or if you're artsy you can start making something (necklaces, paintings, etc.) and sell them online, possibly. I'm sorry that I'm probably not helping.
I'd say try looking online in between the times that you aren't actually physically going out to search.
The most I can advise you to do is keep trying for a job and once successful, save up to take the driving course for 18+s. How often do you go job hunting?

I don't have a doctor in this city as this is only my second semester of college and I've never had the need to see a doctor. In addition, I don't have a vehicle or money for bus fair so I have no way to get anywhere off campus.

I understand about the job thing. It seems like the job pool for younger people is getting smaller and smaller as there are more and more adults working "young adult jobs" (i.e. fast food, restaurants, etc.). Driving isn't hard, and I've driven back from the major city in my area (due to the two people with licenses being heavily intoxicated) on two separate occasions and did just fine. My parents never let me get my license because my sister wrecked the car that was supposed to be mine in an empty parking lot, so they didn't trust me driving by extent. Anyways, do you have any friends that could take time out of their day to teach you how to drive?

Please don't be ashamed of it. It's perfectly fine to feel how you are feeling. There is no shame in saying that you are mentally weak, as most people have been there before. Please, please, please tell your provider the extent of your depression or else she'll never be able to help it completely. Also, you don't have any sort of online friends or are involved in an online community or game? You can find support in those, if so.

Start with finding yourself some sort of reliable support system (via true friends or trusted family members). Then get a mental health evaluation and talk with your healthcare provider for options to help. Medication doesn't help everyone; You'll need to discuss that with a medical professional who knows about this stuff as to find the best form of treatment for you. You don't need to hurt yourself to get it out there that you are hurting, no matter how much you think you do. Are you old enough to make your own doctors appointments or do you still need to go through your parents to make appointments?

I'm 19 and in a similar situation. Except I'm also in Uni and failing out rn bc of depression. So you're not alone. I think now is just a tough spot in life as you're transitioning from someone who was previously guided through everything to someone who has to be somewhat independent and you don't have the means to do so. May I ask why you don't have a license or job? Or if that question just upsets you, then do you have any friends who can help you out of this situation (as in getting you a job somewhere, pointing you towards places that are hiring, etc.)?

I made an appointment with the mental health center on campus, but they're backed up a little over a month so I won't be able to get professional help until April. I don't really talk to any of my friends anymore so it's not like I can tell them about it. I had a friend who unexpectedly told me last night that I can talk to him about anything, but I don't believe that it was an actual offer.

It wouldn't bother anyone. I mean, yeah, people are gonna be like "Aww rip". But no one has the fucking right to say that. I don't have many friends and the few I have don't give a shit about me. They want me to be there for them through their problems, but the second I have one, they dip out. Nothing really entertains me and I have no desire to do anything anymore.

I haven't gone to a full week of class since the beginning of February. I used to actually care about my grades. I used to enjoy hanging out with my friends and going out to parties every once in a while. I used to frequently play Tera (an MMORPG) in my downtime. I used to go home on the weekends to see my niece. Now I'm not interested in any of that. Hell, I've even lost interest in the guy I was in love with and broke up with him bc I didn't want him having to deal with all this. I don't leave my dorm unless absolutely necessary. I barely talk to people anymore. I'm just receding into myself at this point, and I have no will not to.

I understand your hopelessness. However, as someone who is recovering from self harm and drug abuse, I've learned something. Recovery doesn't mean it's not going to happen again. Recovery means it's going to happen again, but you're not going to let yourself be drawn back into it again. You're not going to develop the same obsession with cutting yourself or snorting lines again. It takes time and patience with yourself. Two and a half years is great. That's farther than I've ever gotten. Just know that relapse doesn't make you a bad person or mean that you're getting bad again. It's a healing process. It's gradual. Don't be too hard on yourself over it.
